text: [NCERT Exercise 7] Nitrogen (atomic number 7) and phosphorus (atomic number 15) belong to group 15 of the Periodic Table. Write their electronic configurations. Which of these will be more electronegative and why?

options.text: Nitrogen: $2, 5$; Phosphorus: $2, 8, 5$. Nitrogen is more electronegative because its atomic radius is smaller, allowing the nucleus to attract shared electrons more strongly.
options.rationale: Nitrogen has only 2 shells while phosphorus has 3 shells. The smaller atomic radius of nitrogen results in a stronger effective electrostatic attraction between the nucleus and bonding electrons, making nitrogen significantly more electronegative than phosphorus.

options.text: Nitrogen: $2, 5$; Phosphorus: $2, 8, 5$. Phosphorus is more electronegative because it has more protons in its nucleus.
options.rationale: Although phosphorus has more protons, its extra electron shell increases shielding and atomic distance, which decreases electronegativity down a group.

options.text: Nitrogen: $2, 8$; Phosphorus: $2, 8, 8$. Both have identical electronegativity.
options.rationale: These configurations are for noble gases, not Group 15 elements.

options.text: Neither is electronegative because Group 15 elements are all electropositive metals.
options.rationale: Nitrogen and phosphorus are non-metals with high electronegativity values (N = 3.04, P = 2.19).

solution:
Correct Answer: (A) Nitrogen: $2, 5$; Phosphorus: $2, 8, 5$. Nitrogen is more electronegative because its atomic radius is smaller, allowing the nucleus to attract shared electrons more strongly.

Scientific Principle / Key Concept:
• Electronic configurations:
  - Nitrogen ($Z=7$): $2, 5$ (2 occupied shells: K, L)
  - Phosphorus ($Z=15$): $2, 8, 5$ (3 occupied shells: K, L, M)
• Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract shared pair of electrons toward itself.
• Moving down Group 15 from N to P, an additional electron shell is added, which increases atomic size and nuclear shielding.
• Because nitrogen has a smaller atomic size, its nucleus is closer to the valence shell and exerts a much stronger pull on shared electron pairs.
• Therefore, Nitrogen is more electronegative than Phosphorus.

• Option (B): Incorrect. Distance and shielding overcome extra nuclear charge down a group.
• Option (C): Incorrect electronic configurations.
• Option (D): Incorrect. N and P are non-metals.

text: [NCERT Exercise 8] How does the electronic configuration of an atom relate to its position (period and group) in the Modern Periodic Table?

options.text: The number of occupied electron shells determines the Period number, and the number of valence electrons determines the Group number (Group = valence electrons for 1, 2; Group = $10 + \text{valence electrons}$ for 3 to 8).
options.rationale: Period number = principal energy level / number of shells. Group number reflects valence electrons: 1 valence electron = Group 1; 2 valence electrons = Group 2; 3 to 8 valence electrons = Groups 13 to 18.

options.rationale: Position is governed by electronic configuration (shells and valence electrons), not neutron counts.

options.text: Electronic configuration has no relationship with position in the Modern Periodic Table.

solution:
Correct Answer: (A) The number of occupied electron shells determines the Period number, and the number of valence electrons determines the Group number (Group = valence electrons for 1, 2; Group = $10 + \text{valence electrons}$ for 3 to 8).

• The number of occupied electron shells in an atom determines its period.

• Option (C): Mass is not used.
• Option (D): Electronic configuration is the fundamental basis of the table.

text: [NCERT Exercise 10] Which statement correctly compares and contrasts the arrangement of elements in Mendeléev's Periodic Table versus the Modern Periodic Table?

options.text: Mendeléev's Table is based on increasing atomic masses with 8 groups (divided into sub-groups A and B), could not position isotopes, and had anomalous inverted mass pairs; the Modern Periodic Table is based on increasing atomic numbers with 18 distinct vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods, naturally accommodating isotopes and resolving all mass inversions.
options.rationale: The foundational difference is atomic mass vs atomic number. The Modern Table expanded the structure to 18 independent columns and 7 periods, resolving isotopes, anomalous pairs (Co/Ni, Te/I), and transition element placement.

options.text: Mendeléev's Table used atomic numbers, while the Modern Table reverted to atomic masses.
options.rationale: Mendeléev used atomic masses; the Modern Table uses atomic numbers.

options.text: Both tables have identical 18 groups and placed noble gases in Group 1 with alkali metals.
options.rationale: Mendeléev's original table had 8 groups with no noble gases initially; noble gases were placed in Group 18 in the Modern Table.

options.text: Mendeléev's Table arranged elements into octaves of musical notes, while the Modern Table uses atomic volume triads.
options.rationale: Musical octaves were used by Newlands, not Mendeléev.

solution:
Correct Answer: (A) Mendeléev's Table is based on increasing atomic masses with 8 groups (divided into sub-groups A and B), could not position isotopes, and had anomalous inverted mass pairs; the Modern Periodic Table is based on increasing atomic numbers with 18 distinct vertical groups and 7 horizontal periods, naturally accommodating isotopes and resolving all mass inversions.

Scientific Principle / Key Concept:
Comparison:
1. Basis of Classification:
• Mendeléev's Table: Atomic mass (Properties are periodic function of atomic masses).
• Modern Periodic Table: Atomic number (Properties are periodic function of atomic numbers).
2. Structure:
• Mendeléev: 8 Groups (subdivided into A and B sub-groups) and 6 Periods.
• Modern Table: 18 Vertical columns (Groups) and 7 Horizontal rows (Periods).
3. Anomalies & Isotopes:
• Mendeléev could not assign a fixed place to hydrogen or isotopes, and had anomalous pairs (Co before Ni, Te before I).
• Modern Table places isotopes in the same position and puts Co ($Z=27$) before Ni ($Z=28$) without anomaly.
